records.name: Holy Family Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish in Manayunk on Hermitage Street with Sunday and weekday Masses and a Religious Education program for children.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or call the parish office at 215-482-0450 to ask about Religious Education or the summer camp. Confirm the camp is running before you plan on it.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9 and 11 am, Saturday vigil Mass at 4 pm, and Monday to Friday Mass at 9 am. Confession is Saturdays at 3 pm and Sundays at 8:30 and 10:30 am. The 9 am Sunday Mass is livestreamed.

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The site does not list fees for Religious Education or the summer camp.

access.notes: The Hermitage Street entrance is not wheelchair accessible. The parking lot entrance has one step. Handicap parking is in the Fowler Street lot.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass at 9 or 11 am, or call the parish office at 215-482-0450 to ask about Religious Education.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish lists a phone number and an email. Its online form is for becoming a registered parishioner.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. The 9 am Sunday Mass is livestreamed on the parish website, so you can watch before you come. The site does not say how long Mass lasts or what happens after it, so call ahead with questions.
first_visit_tips: Park in the Fowler Street lot, where the handicap spaces are, or on Hermitage Street.
Use the parking lot entrance. The Hermitage Street door is not wheelchair accessible, and the lot entrance has one step.
The rectory office is open Monday to Thursday, 8:30 am to 3 pm, if you have questions.

records.notes: Corrections to tier 1: the parish Mass schedule page lists weekday Mass at 9 am (tier 1 said 8 am), and the parish programs page lists only Religious Education, so the child care claim is removed from the summary. A search result pointed to a summer camp page on the parish site (Camp Acaraho, listed for ages 3 to 13), but I did not open it, so the camp is unconfirmed; the same search also pointed to an August 2024 CBS News Philadelphia report that the parish child care center was closing. Neither was opened or verified. The newest dated item on the parish site is a 2024 Holy Week post, so no last_sign_of_life is set. Status stays probably_active because the site is working and posts current Mass times, but a reviewer should look at this one.

records.name: Holy Innocents Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish in Hunting Park with Masses in English, Spanish and Vietnamese. It also runs a food pantry and a Monday afternoon group for seniors.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in English, Spanish or Vietnamese. The parish also runs a food pantry (last Thursday and Friday of the month), a senior group that meets Monday afternoons, and religious education for children and youth. Adults who want to join the Catholic Church can ask about OCIA classes.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm in English and 6:30 pm in Spanish. Sunday Masses at 7:30 and 10 am in English, noon in Spanish, and 5 pm in Vietnamese. Weekday Mass at 6:30 and 8 am, or 8 am only in summer. Confession Saturdays from 3:30 to 4:30 pm. The St. Joan of Arc worship site has Sunday Masses at 9 am in English and 11:30 am in Spanish.

locations.label: Parish church
locations.address: L St. and Hunting Park Ave.

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The site does not list fees for religious education.

first_step.how: Come to any listed Mass, or call the rectory at 215-743-2600 or email holyinnocents@comcast.net to ask about religious education, youth groups, the food pantry, or OCIA.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish publishes a phone number and an email. The adult faith classes page is dated 2024, so those details may be out of date.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. Sunday Masses run at 7:30 and 10 am in English, noon in Spanish and 5 pm in Vietnamese, so choose the one in your language. The site does not say how long Mass takes or what happens afterward, so call the rectory with questions before you go.
first_visit_tips: Weekday Mass in summer is at 8 am only.
The Saturday vigil is at 4:30 pm in English and 6:30 pm in Spanish. Confession is Saturdays from 3:30 to 4:30 pm.
The church is at L Street and Hunting Park Avenue. The rectory is at 1337 E. Hunting Park Avenue.

records.notes: The faith formation page gives class start dates in September and October 2024, so the PREP, youth, young adult and OCIA details may be out of date. Call to confirm. Liturgy of the Word for Pre-K to 3rd grade runs during the 10 am and noon Masses from September to May, per that page. The St. Joan of Arc worship site has no street address on the parish site, so none is added. The site has no accessibility information. The footer shows 2023 as a copyright year, which is not used as evidence. The newest dated item found is from 2024, so no last_sign_of_life is set; status stays probably_active because the site posts current weekly Mass times. The Food Pantry and senior group were added from the organizations page.

records.name: Holy Name of Jesus Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish in Fishtown with Sunday Masses at 8 and 11 am, a Saturday vigil, and weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass. The Archdiocese page lists the parish school but no other public programs.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 and 11 am, Saturday Vigil Mass at 4:30 pm, and weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 8 am. Confession Saturdays 3:30 to 4:15 pm.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, or call the rectory to ask about parish groups.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the rectory phone is listed on the Archdiocese page. The parish's own site could not be read, so this rests on that listing.

records.notes: Not deepened. The parish's own site could not be read: the old domain returns a 301 redirect to holynameofjesusparish.org, and that address fails with a TLS certificate error on every attempt (three tries). This record is carried over from tier 1 only, so it stays research_tier 1 until the site can be read. Re-run this one when the site is reachable, and check whether the redirect target is the parish's current site.

records.name: Holy Redeemer Chinese Catholic Church
records.summary: A Chinese Catholic parish in Chinatown at 915 Vine Street with Sunday Masses in Cantonese, English and Mandarin.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in Cantonese, English or Mandarin. Ask about RCIA (the baptism prep classes), Cantonese and Mandarin Bible study, the Cantonese choir, or the Sunday religion classes for children. Lector and Eucharistic minister roles need no previous experience.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 10 am in Cantonese, 11:15 am in English and 12:30 pm in Mandarin. Monday to Friday Mass is at 8:30 am. The Cantonese and Mandarin Masses are livestreamed.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass in the language you prefer. To ask about RCIA or the children's religion classes, call the church office at 215-922-0999 or use the contact form on the parish website.
first_step.basis: The parish says newcomers can start with RCIA, and a September 2026 post says lector and Eucharistic minister roles need no previous experience. The site also lists ways to contact the parish.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday Mass is offered in Cantonese, English or Mandarin, and the Cantonese and Mandarin Masses are livestreamed. The Mass is free to attend. The site does not say how long Mass lasts or what a first visit feels like, so the church office is the best place to ask questions.
first_visit_tips: Each Sunday Mass is in a different language, so pick the time that matches the language you want.
Call 215-922-0999 or use the contact form before your first visit if you have questions.
RCIA is the baptism preparation class. Ask about it when you call.

records.notes: Phone corrected: the parish contact page lists 215.922.0999 for the church and school. The tier 1 value, 215-563-4145, is the number the site lists for St. John the Evangelist. The site publishes no general email address, only a contact form. Dated items on the site: a lector and Eucharistic minister post and several news posts dated September 11, 2026, and weekly bulletins dated August 16 to September 13, 2026. Zoom meeting IDs and passcodes on the site were not recorded. Children's religion class details are only available by contacting the church administrator, as the site says.

records.name: Holy Trinity Bethlehem Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on West Rockland Street that worships on Sunday, holds a weekly Wednesday prayer and Bible study, and welcomes people to come as they are.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship in person or online, join the Wednesday prayer and Bible study at 4 pm, or the short Friday morning prayer at 10:45 am.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, also streamed live on YouTube, Facebook and Zoom. Wednesday prayer and Bible study at 4 pm. Friday morning prayer at 10:45 am, about 15 minutes.

first_step.how: Attend Sunday worship at 11 am in person or online, or join the Wednesday 4 pm prayer and Bible study. Use the contact form on the church website to ask anything first.
first_step.basis: The church says all are welcome to come as they are, and its site has a visit page and a contact form for people who want to ask first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship is at 11 am in the sanctuary, and it is also streamed live on YouTube, Facebook and Zoom, so you can watch from home first. The site does not say how long the service runs, what to bring, or whether you need to sign up. The Friday morning prayer is about 15 minutes, and the site says all are welcome to pray with the church.
first_visit_tips: The church is at 1100 W. Rockland Street in the Logan neighborhood.
The church says to come as you are.
The church office is open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 5 pm, if you want to call before you come.

records.notes: Email corrected to info@htbpresbyterian.org, the address on the church's own contact page. The tier 1 value, htbpres@verizon.net, came from the presbytery listing. The contact page also shows placeholder details (a Florida address, a 555 phone number and a placeholder email) that do not match this church, so they were not used. The site has no dated news, and the copyright line and an old 2020 streaming note are not evidence of current activity. No children's program, parking or accessibility information is on the site. Zoom details were not recorded. The Facebook and YouTube links on the site go to a pastor's page and a search page, so no social link is recorded.

records.name: Hope for Tomorrow
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that gives out food, diapers, clothing, and water to families in need. It also runs a summer camp, a college scholarship, and holiday baskets and toys.
records.what_you_do: Ask about the Cupboard food program, the diaper program (run with the Delaware Valley Diaper Bank), clothing, water bottles, the summer camp, the undergraduate scholarship, and holiday baskets and toys. The site does not say how to sign up, so call first.

first_step.how: Call (215) 844-8389 and ask how to sign up for the Cupboard food, diaper, clothing, or summer camp programs.
first_step.basis: The programs are listed on the site, but it does not say who qualifies, how to sign up, or when programs run, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit or list hours, so the first step is a phone call to the number on the site. Ask what each program needs and who can get help, since the site does not say who qualifies.
first_visit_tips: Call before you travel, since the site does not list office or distribution hours.
The site has a contact form but no email address.

records.notes: The programs page names each program but gives no eligibility rules, sign-up steps, hours, distribution days, or costs, so newcomer friendliness stays at 2. The diaper program is run with the Delaware Valley Diaper Bank per the site; that group has no URL on this site, so it is not added as a lead. The site footer shows a 2020 copyright and the only other dates are from 2014, so the site may not be updated often. Status stays probably_active because the site is working and lists programs, and an IRS filing from 2026 was found in tier 1; confidence is low. The contact name Omar S Galloway comes from IRS and tier 1 data and does not appear on the site. The Family Care Program is listed on the programs page with no description.

records.name: Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A statewide group that works for affordable housing and eviction prevention. It follows state lawmaking, posts legislative updates, supports housing workers with training, and invites members of the public to take action on housing policy.
records.what_you_do: Read the legislative updates, take action on housing bills, and sign up for the newsletter. Members get free educational webinars and a discount on the Homes Within Reach Conference. Volunteers can serve on committees and boards, but the volunteer page does not say how to apply.

schedule.text: Legislative updates and news posts come out about once a month. No regular meeting time is listed.

cost.text: The site does not state a membership fee or dues amount.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the monthly newsletter, or call 215-576-7044 or email info@housingalliancepa.org to ask how to become a member.
first_step.basis: The updates and newsletter are open to the public, but the site does not explain the steps to join as a member or volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: There is no meeting to attend, so a first visit means reading. The group posts legislative updates and news on its website about once a month. Members get free webinars and a discount on the Homes Within Reach Conference, which is set for December 14 to 16, 2026.
first_visit_tips: Read the most recent legislative update on the website to see what the group is tracking.
Ask staff by phone or email which kind of membership fits you, since the site does not list membership levels or fees.
The office address on the site is a mailing address, so call before you visit.

records.notes: Corrections to tier 1: the cost text said membership has an annual fee, but neither the homepage nor the membership page states any fee, so the cost text now says that. The conference dates moved out of schedule text because they are a dated event, and the schedule is now recurring monthly updates with no meeting time. The contact name 'The Organization' is removed because it is not a person's name. Recent dated items: a July 23, 2026 legislative update, a June 2026 legislative update and a June 2026 message, and a May 28, 2026 update. The volunteer page lists committee and board members but does not say how to apply. The homepage says Phyllis Chamberlain is leaving after ten years and Beth Sturman will serve as interim executive director; this is not in the record. The events page links to the 2026 conference and a summit but gives no dates for the summit.
